rulings.model: IRS line 1 excludes you or your spouse from tax family size if someone can claim you or your spouse as a dependent; the restatement just adds the person count plus claimed dependents.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope — the dependency exclusion is enforced at the return level: sa.dependent records whether someone can claim the filer or spouse, and its refusal on sa.standardraw propagates to f1040.line12e and the whole return (i1040gi pp. 34–35). A witness with a Form 1095-A and sa.dependent true was checked on 2026-11-01 and f1040.line24 is refused. The render review does not show the return-wide refusal.

rulings.restated: Add household helper "Number of people on the return (you, and your spouse if filing jointly)" and helper "Dependents you claim".
rulings.model: IRS line 1 is tax family size, and the instructions say 'you or your spouse is not included in the tax family size calculation' if someone can claim you as a dependent; the restatement counts all persons on the return plus dependents.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope — the instruction that a claimable filer or spouse is not included in the tax family size (i8962 p. 8) is enforced at the return level: sa.dependent answers whether someone can claim the filer or spouse, and its refusal on sa.standardraw propagates to f1040.line12e and the whole return (i1040gi pp. 34–35), so no return with a claimable filer or spouse computes line 1. A witness with a Form 1095-A and sa.dependent true was checked on 2026-11-01: f1040.line24 is refused. The render review of f8962 does not show the return-wide refusal.

rulings.restated: Add household helper "Number of people on the return (you, and your spouse if filing jointly)" and helper "Dependents you claim".
rulings.model: The line 1 instructions say that if someone can claim you, or your spouse on a joint return, as a dependent, that person is not included in the tax family size calculation; the restatement adds the filer and spouse unconditionally.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; screen sa.dependent (root S2). i8962 p. 8, Line 1, "If you checked the “Someone can claim you as a dependent” box, or if you are filing jointly and you checked the “Someone can claim your spouse as a dependent” box on your tax return, you or your spouse is not included in the tax family size calculation". A return on which you or your spouse can be claimed is never completed: sa.dependent ("Can someone claim you or your spouse as a dependent for 2025 ...", forms/2025/sa.yaml) refuses f1040.line12e on every return, and D1 keeps the claimable filer refused. On the returns computed nobody on the return can be claimed, so everyone on it is in the tax family, as the restatement says. Re-checked this round on stage18.married_in_2025_single (a completed fixture; line 24 $3,560) with one answer changed by the adjudicator (constructed variants, not fixtures): sa.dependent true refuses Form 1040 lines 12e, 16 and 37 with gate sa.dependent.

rulings.model: IRS line 24 must be -0- when you are not an applicable taxpayer, including married filing separately without an exception; the applicable helper checks only income or the Marketplace estimate, omitting the joint-return and dependency requirements.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope — married filing separately is refused for the whole return by s3.mfs, and Part V (the alternative calculation for year of marriage) by f8962.marriage; the applicable helper's income and Marketplace-estimate limbs are the only reachable ones. The render review does not show the return-wide refusal.

rulings.model: The IRS applicable-taxpayer test also requires that 'no one can claim you as a dependent for 2025' and, if married at year end, that you 'must file a joint return'; the restatement's applicable helper tests only line 5 at least 100 or the Marketplace estimate exception.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope — the applicable-taxpayer conditions the model names are enforced elsewhere: a claimable filer or spouse is refused at the return level through sa.dependent (sa.standardraw → f1040.line12e), and married filing separately is refused for the whole return by s3.mfs. The applicable helper covers the income and Marketplace-estimate limbs, and the estimate question now carries the intentional/reckless misreporting disqualifier (T-162e). The render review does not show the return-wide refusals.

rulings.model: The IRS applicable-taxpayer test also requires that no one can claim you as a dependent and, if married at the end of 2025, a joint return unless an exception applies; the restatement reduces it to line 5 at least 100 or the Marketplace estimate exception.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; screens s3.mfs (root S1, stated in full in the Claude render ruling of 11(a), fixr2/render.f8962.json) and sa.dependent (root S2). f8962 p. 1, item A, "You cannot take the PTC if your filing status is married filing separately unless you qualify for an exception"; i8962 p. 16, Not an applicable taxpayer, "If you are not an applicable taxpayer because you are using filing status married filing separately and Exception 2, earlier, does not apply to you, you cannot take the PTC ... enter -0- on line 24"; i8962 p. 3, "2. No one can claim you as a dependent for the year." Both conditions the reviewer names are refused for the whole return: scope.ready on s3.mfs and Form 1040 line 12e on sa.dependent, so on every completed return the applicable-taxpayer test reduces to line 5 and the estimate exception (with its advance payments), as restated; the alien branch stays refused by f8962.alien_branch. Re-checked this round on stage18.married_in_2025_single (a completed fixture; line 24 $3,560) with one answer changed by the adjudicator (constructed variants, not fixtures): f1040.status mfs refuses scope.ready and Form 1040 line 37 with gate s3.mfs; sa.dependent true refuses Form 1040 lines 12e, 16 and 37 with gate sa.dependent.

rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "You are an applicable taxpayer (line 5 at least 100, or the Marketplace estimate exception)" = false → helper "Year parameter sales.zero"] [helper "You are an applicable taxpayer (line 5 at least 100, or the Marketplace estimate exception)" = true → helper "The PTC allowed: line 11, column (e), or lines 12 through 23, column (e), added"]
rulings.model: The restatement treats line 5 >= 100 or the Marketplace estimate as sufficient for an applicable taxpayer, but IRS says if married at the end of 2025 you generally must file a joint return, and you cannot take the PTC with married filing separately unless an exception applies.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; screen s3.mfs (root S1). f8962 p. 1, item A, "You cannot take the PTC if your filing status is married filing separately unless you qualify for an exception"; i8962 p. 16, Not an applicable taxpayer, "If you are not an applicable taxpayer because you are using filing status married filing separately and Exception 2, earlier, does not apply to you, you cannot take the PTC ... enter -0- on line 24". The reviewer's point is the married-filing-separately bar (and the joint-return expectation for someone married at the end of 2025). No married filing separately return is completed: scope.ready refuses on s3.mfs (forms/2025/s3.yaml, scope.yaml, cite i1040gi p. 14), Exception 2 included, as D1 keeps; the rendering's form note says so. Re-checked this round: stage18.married_in_2025_single with f1040.status set to mfs (constructed by the adjudicator from the fixture, not a fixture) evaluates to a refusal at scope.ready and Form 1040 line 37 with gate s3.mfs.

rulings.restated: Choose — [line 5 ≥ 0 (a count) and line 5 < 200 (a count) → helper "Table 5 limitation, line 5 below 200"] [line 5 ≥ 200 (a count) and line 5 < 300 (a count) → helper "Table 5 limitation, line 5 below 300"] [line 5 ≥ 300 (a count) and line 5 < 400 (a count) → helper "Table 5 limitation, line 5 below 400"] [line 5 ≥ 400 (a count) → line 27]
rulings.model: The IRS line 28 instructions say that if you are self-employed and claiming the self-employed health insurance deduction, see Pub. 974 for the amount to enter; the restatement only uses the Table 5 limitation and has no adjustment or refusal for that case.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope — i8962 p. 18, Line 28, "If you are self-employed and are claiming the self-employed health insurance deduction, see Self-Employed Health Insurance Deduction and PTC in Pub. 974 for the amount to enter on line 28.". A return claiming the self-employed health insurance deduction with the premium tax credit is refused: sc.hi_screen (forms/2025/sc.yaml) asks whether "the insurance was obtained through the Marketplace and advance payments of the premium tax credit were made or you are claiming the premium tax credit" and refuses sc.f7206_line1 and the return, so the Pub. 974 line 28 amount cannot arise on a computed return. The restatement is faithful to the project's Table 5 line; the omission the model names is handled by that screen, not by line 28.

rulings.restated: Enter the smaller of line 27 or line 28.
rulings.model: IRS line 29 says 'If line 28 is blank, enter the amount from line 27'; the restatement only says enter the smaller of line 27 or line 28 and omits the blank-line-28 case.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; i8962 p. 17, Line 29, "If line 28 is blank, enter the amount from line 27". For line 5 at 400 or more the project sets line 28 to line 27 and hides it (f8962.show_28), so the smaller of the two is line 27 on every return.

rulings.restated: (helper "A policy shared with another tax family, or a divorce or separation in 2025 with a shared policy" = true or helper "A joint return with Marketplace coverage before the first full month of a 2025 marriage" = true)
rulings.model: The IRS asks whether you are allocating policy amounts or 'do you want to use the alternative calculation for year of marriage'; the restatement makes line 9 Yes merely for a joint return with pre-marriage Marketplace coverage, regardless of the election or other Table 4 eligibility.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; screens f8962.alloc and f8962.marriage (root S4). f8962 p. 1, line 9, "Are you allocating policy amounts with another taxpayer or do you want to use the alternative calculation for year of marriage? See instructions."; i8962 p. 12, "You need to allocate policy amounts ... if: 1. The policy covered at least one individual in your tax family and at least one individual in another tax family; and 2. Either: ..."; p. 13, Table 4. The reviewer is right that the restatement makes line 9 Yes on the facts that open Part IV or Part V (f8962.alloc; f8962.marriage, a joint return with coverage before the first full month of a 2025 marriage) instead of condition 2 and the Part V election. Every Yes refuses lines 24 and 25 (stage18.refuse.allocation, gate f8962.alloc, re-evaluated this round; stage18.refuse.year_of_marriage, gate f8962.marriage), as D1 and D5 decide, so where the facts hold and the source would answer No the project refuses instead of computing: an over-refusal, never a wrong amount. This round's rewording of f8962.alloc (BUG-0237) adds a policy whose Form 1095-A went only to someone else and a child you claim whom someone else enrolled, both cases of condition 1 that the source requires to be allocated when condition 2(b) holds ("The other tax family received a Form 1095-A for the policy that includes a member of your tax family"); it still asks condition 1 only, as before, so the over-refusal is unchanged in kind and no computed amount changes.
